newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products steady except weaker gas oil.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products steady except weaker gas oil.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were steady apart from weaker gas oil.
Gasoline prices were steady but several traders said the arbitrage was very close to being open to the U.S., which could support an otherwise balanced Med market.
"There is actually a flow of product going to the U.S. or at least all the companies are carefully watching the arb," said one Italian trader.
She said there was demand for eastern Mediterranean destinations, with low octane and high octane material wanted in Lebanon, and premium unleaded into the Ukraine.
Demand was also perking up in Portugal for small amounts of super unleaded and premium unleaded, and into Turkey and ex-Yugoslovian countries, she said.
"Undoubtedly the values for gasoline in the States are soaring and since the Med is fairly balanced, the arb is probably open," said another Italian trader.
Premium unleaded cargoes traded at $233/$234 cif, traders said.
Naphtha prices were steady in quiet action. Traders said there was talk of loading some Algerian cargoes together to optimize freight rates, but this was not confirmed.
Gas oil prices slipped very slightly, but traders saw good demand for high sulphur grades.
Demand was reported into Turkey, India and Tunisia for high sulphur, but a low sulphur diesel bid in Genoa was heard at Dec +$14 cif against a prompt Algerian cargo offered a dollar above that.

Traders looking to cover India's December tender sought high sulphur supplies from the Italian islands, Lavera and Constanza, because these ports were able to handle the larger vessels needed to make the arbitrage work. "The arbitrage to Asia is not wide open -- it's selectively open," a trader said.
